title: Gulf War III or Cold War II: Iran Truth and Consequences
summary: Hoover Institution fellows call the 2026 Iran war Gulf War III within Cold War II, not WW3, expect it to be short, and weigh the oil shock and how China reads US depleted stocks.

assertions.quote: No, it's not World War III, though I don't think it's a stupid question
It's something that takes weeks as opposed to what happened after 2003

verdicts.note: Major US strikes wound down within a few months amid talk of a deal, but no durable settlement was reached and renewed fighting remained possible.
The 2026 war ran from 28 February to a ceasefire on 8 April, about forty days, though talks were unsettled and a resumption was possible.

assertions.quote: It becomes World War III if another major power comes in on the side of Iran, and no one's doing that, not even China
then the world is going to be on the receiving end of one of the biggest energy shocks of our lifetimes.
we should be acting when the United States has depleted its capabilities before they've been replaced, and while it is entangled

verdicts.note: DDIS says the Ukraine war has diverted US focus from the China threat; it says nothing here about Middle East wars or munitions.

assertions.quote: under the Biden administration, the axis of aggressors coalesced. They were the protagonists, they were setting the terms.

verdicts.note: DoD finds China-North Korea relations 'notably cool' in 2024, with Beijing distancing itself from Pyongyang's support for Russia's war; together with no formal China-Russia alliance and a modest China-Iran link, this cuts against four states 'acting together'.

DDIS reports China, Iran and North Korea all supplying Russia's war and China and Russia leading a group seeking to cut US influence, but describes support and alignment, not four states acting together.
EFIS describes close China-Russia alignment and North Korean arms and troops for Russia, but says Russia abandoned Iran in its hour of need, which undercuts the idea of four states acting together.

US intelligence finds selective cooperation among China, Russia, Iran and North Korea that adds to the threat, but calls it limited and mainly bilateral and says 'adversary alignment' overstates its depth.

assertions.quote: So I think we can probably rule out a Taiwan crisis this year. Next year, I'm not so sure.

verdicts.note: As of October 2026 China had not blockaded or attacked Taiwan and a Trump-Xi summit eased tensions, though the year is not over.
A linked Metaculus question puts a Chinese attack on or blockade of Taiwan in 2026 at 2%.
Polymarket priced a China-Taiwan military clash before 2027 at 3.8% and a blockade of Taiwan in 2026 at 2.55%.
US intelligence expects China to stay short of conflict in 2026 but notes it has at times expanded the scope, size and pace of operations around Taiwan, so pressure short of war continues.
CFR's experts gave a severe cross-strait crisis caused by intensified Chinese pressure an even chance of occurring in 2026, so they did not rule one out.

assertions.quote: But I think in terms of the scope of this war, the geographic scope of this war, it's waning.
we might have fired about one-fifth of our interceptor stockpile in three days

verdicts.note: War games and US officials report that key munitions would run short within weeks in a war with China, and the 2026 Middle East fighting drew interceptors down fast.
In every CSIS iteration the US used up its entire global inventory of about 450 LRASM anti-ship missiles in the first week of the war.
US intelligence says exquisite high-end capabilities are expensive and slow to make and cannot be replenished at scale in a long high-intensity war, a general point that does not measure US stocks.
